title: TUTORIAL DE RUEDA DE CASINO. "LA MEGA RUEDA IMBATIBLE DE CASINO". RETOMANDO EL SON #tutorial

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher acts as a caller, shouting out the names of the Rueda de Casino figures to a group of dancers. He does not provide verbal instructions or demonstrations, but rather leads the group through a continuous, fast-paced sequence of moves.

lesson_structure.note: Title card and promotional text for a Guinness World Record attempt.
The group performs a continuous, fast-paced Rueda de Casino sequence.

steps_taught.name: Dile que no
steps_taught.description: The basic step to break the hold and change partners.

steps_taught.name: Exhibela
steps_taught.description: A move where the leader shows off the follower.

steps_taught.name: Culebra
steps_taught.description: A snake-like movement where dancers weave through the circle.

steps_taught.name: Sombrero
steps_taught.description: A move where the leader places their hands on the follower's shoulders.

steps_taught.name: Dame una
steps_taught.description: A command to switch partners in the circle.

what_works: The clear, rhythmic calling of the steps helps the dancers stay in sync.
The consistent, high-energy music keeps the pace steady.
what_hinders: The lack of verbal explanation or breakdown makes it difficult for beginners to learn the steps.
The fast pace and complex sequence are challenging for those not already familiar with the figures.

evidence_segments.observation: The group begins the Rueda de Casino sequence, moving in a circle.
The teacher calls out 'Mujeres' and 'Exhibela' while the dancers execute the moves.
The dancers perform 'Abajo' and then 'Desplazate' as called by the teacher.
The dancers execute 'Culebra' as the teacher calls it.
The dancers perform 'Dile que no' and 'Guapea' in response to the calls.
The dancers execute 'Sombrero' as the teacher calls it.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher uses a 'calling' method, where he shouts the names of the figures to a group of dancers who are already proficient in the dance, rather than teaching the steps to beginners.
